Title: In E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982), which candy does Elliott use to lay a trail for E.T.?
AnswerDetails: Elliott lures E.T. into the house with a trail of Reese's Pieces, and the candy's sales jumped after the film opened.

Title: In Back to the Future (1985), what speed must the DeLorean reach to travel through time?
AnswerDetails: Doc Brown's time machine jumps when it hits 88 mph, powered by 1.21 gigawatts from the flux capacitor.

Title: In Ghostbusters (1984), what giant figure does Gozer take after Ray tries to think of something harmless?
AnswerDetails: Ray pictures a mascot from his childhood, and a building-sized Stay Puft Marshmallow Man stomps through Manhattan.

Title: In Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981), which creatures is Indiana Jones famously afraid of?
AnswerDetails: "Snakes. Why'd it have to be snakes?" The Well of Souls is full of them, which is exactly what Indy dreads.

Title: In The Karate Kid (1984), what is the name of the dojo where Daniel's tormentors train?
AnswerDetails: Johnny Lawrence and his friends train at Cobra Kai under the ruthless sensei John Kreese.

Title: In Ferris Bueller's Day Off (1986), which car do Ferris and Cameron borrow from Cameron's father?
AnswerDetails: Cameron's father's prized red 1961 Ferrari 250 GT California gets a day in Chicago it was never meant to have.

Title: In The Goonies (1985), whose lost pirate treasure are the kids hunting for?
AnswerDetails: An old treasure map leads the Goonies under the Oregon coast in search of One-Eyed Willy's ship and gold.

Title: In Die Hard (1988), which Los Angeles skyscraper does Hans Gruber's gang take over?
AnswerDetails: John McClane is visiting the Nakatomi Corporation's Christmas party when the building is seized. Fox Plaza stood in for it.

Title: In Gremlins (1984), what is the name of the mogwai that Billy receives as a gift?
AnswerDetails: Gizmo is the gentle mogwai; Stripe is the mohawked leader of the gremlins that spawn after the rules are broken.

Title: In Big (1988), Tom Hanks and Robert Loggia play "Chopsticks" on a giant floor piano in which New York toy store?
AnswerDetails: The walking-piano duet was filmed at FAO Schwarz on Fifth Avenue and became one of the decade's best-loved scenes.

Title: In which 1984 film does Arnold Schwarzenegger first say "I'll be back"?
AnswerDetails: The line comes at a police station front desk in The Terminator, shortly before he drives a car through the doors.

Title: Which 1983 film's climactic shoot-out features the line "Say hello to my little friend!"?
AnswerDetails: Al Pacino's Tony Montana bellows it in the climactic shoot-out of Brian De Palma's Scarface.

Title: In Wall Street (1987), which character declares that "greed, for lack of a better word, is good"?
AnswerDetails: Michael Douglas's corporate raider Gordon Gekko makes the speech at a shareholders' meeting; Douglas won Best Actor.

Title: In Back to the Future, who says "Roads? Where we're going, we don't need roads"?
AnswerDetails: Christopher Lloyd's Doc Brown delivers the final line of the film before the DeLorean lifts off.

Title: In which 1980 horror film does Jack Nicholson push his face through an axed door and announce "Here's Johnny!"?
AnswerDetails: Jack Torrance borrows Ed McMahon's introduction for Johnny Carson as he axes through the bathroom door.

Title: In which 1982 film does little Carol Anne announce "They're here"?
AnswerDetails: Carol Anne Freeling says it in front of a static-filled television set, and the spirits arrive soon after.

Title: In The Princess Bride (1987), which character keeps exclaiming "Inconceivable!"?
AnswerDetails: Wallace Shawn's Vizzini overuses the word until Inigo remarks, "I do not think it means what you think it means."

Title: Which 1989 comedy gave the world the motto "Be excellent to each other"?
AnswerDetails: Bill and Ted's motto, along with "Party on, dudes!", becomes the founding wisdom of the future society that sends Rufus back to help them.

Title: Clint Eastwood's line "Go ahead, make my day" comes from which Dirty Harry film?
AnswerDetails: The line is from Sudden Impact, the fourth Dirty Harry film and the only one Eastwood also directed.

Title: In When Harry Met Sally... (1989), the diner customer who says "I'll have what she's having" is played by whose mother?
AnswerDetails: Estelle Reiner, mother of director Rob Reiner, delivers the punchline in Katz's Delicatessen.

Title: Who played Sarah Connor in The Terminator (1984)?
AnswerDetails: Linda Hamilton played the waitress Sarah Connor, a role she returned to in Terminator 2 in 1991.

Title: Who played the title "bio-exorcist" in Beetlejuice (1988)?
AnswerDetails: Michael Keaton played Betelgeuse for director Tim Burton a year before the two made Batman.

Title: Who played Princess Leia in Return of the Jedi (1983)?
AnswerDetails: Carrie Fisher played Leia across the original trilogy; Karen Allen was Marion in Raiders of the Lost Ark.

Title: In Tootsie (1982), Dustin Hoffman's out-of-work actor disguises himself as a woman to land a role in what?
AnswerDetails: Michael Dorsey becomes "Dorothy Michaels" and wins a part on the hospital soap Southwest General.

Title: Who played Detroit detective Axel Foley in Beverly Hills Cop (1984)?
AnswerDetails: Eddie Murphy's Axel Foley follows a case to Beverly Hills; the film was among the biggest hits of 1984.

Title: In Lethal Weapon (1987), who played Martin Riggs opposite Danny Glover's Roger Murtaugh?
AnswerDetails: Mel Gibson and Danny Glover went on to make a whole series of Lethal Weapon films together.

Title: Who played the android Bishop in Aliens (1986)?
AnswerDetails: Lance Henriksen played Bishop. Michael Biehn was Hicks, Bill Paxton was Hudson and Paul Reiser was Burke.

Title: Which actor played Dr. Peter Venkman in Ghostbusters (1984)?
AnswerDetails: Bill Murray played Venkman; co-writers Dan Aykroyd and Harold Ramis played Ray Stantz and Egon Spengler.

Title: In Who Framed Roger Rabbit (1988), who played the toon-hating detective Eddie Valiant?
AnswerDetails: Bob Hoskins acted mostly against empty space; Christopher Lloyd played the villain, Judge Doom.

Title: Which future star played Elliott's little sister Gertie in E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial?
AnswerDetails: Drew Barrymore was six when filming began and steals several scenes, including teaching E.T. to talk.

Title: Which studio made the animated musical The Little Mermaid (1989)?
AnswerDetails: Walt Disney Feature Animation made it, and its success launched what fans call the Disney Renaissance.

Title: Which actor was originally cast as Marty McFly and filmed for weeks before being replaced by Michael J. Fox?
AnswerDetails: Eric Stoltz shot several weeks as Marty before the filmmakers recast the part with Michael J. Fox.

Title: Who directed Raging Bull (1980), the black-and-white boxing drama starring Robert De Niro?
AnswerDetails: Martin Scorsese directed it, and De Niro won Best Actor for playing the middleweight Jake LaMotta.

Title: Who directed Batman (1989), starring Michael Keaton and Jack Nicholson?
AnswerDetails: Tim Burton directed Batman a year after Beetlejuice; Joel Schumacher took over the series in 1995.

Title: Which actor was first offered Indiana Jones but had to turn it down because of his TV series Magnum, P.I.?
AnswerDetails: Tom Selleck was contracted to Magnum, P.I., and the role went to Harrison Ford.

Title: Disney's Tron (1982) was a landmark for which filmmaking technique?
AnswerDetails: Tron was one of the first feature films to use computer-generated imagery at length, blended with backlit animation.

Title: Who directed the Studio Ghibli film My Neighbor Totoro (1988)?
AnswerDetails: Hayao Miyazaki directed Totoro; his Ghibli colleague Isao Takahata's Grave of the Fireflies was released alongside it.

Title: Akira Kurosawa's 1985 epic Ran adapts which Shakespeare play?
AnswerDetails: Ran moves King Lear to feudal Japan. Kurosawa had adapted Macbeth decades earlier as Throne of Blood (1957).

Title: Who directed The Shining (1980)?
AnswerDetails: Stanley Kubrick adapted Stephen King's novel, famously demanding many takes of key scenes.

Title: Which director made the 1986 remake of The Fly, starring Jeff Goldblum?
AnswerDetails: David Cronenberg directed The Fly; John Carpenter had made his own celebrated horror remake, The Thing, in 1982.

Title: Which film was the highest-grossing release of the 1980s?
AnswerDetails: E.T. overtook Star Wars as the highest-grossing film ever and held that record until Jurassic Park in 1993.

Title: Which biographical epic won Best Picture for 1982, beating E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial?
AnswerDetails: Richard Attenborough's Gandhi won eight Oscars, including Best Picture and Best Actor for Ben Kingsley.

Title: Oliver Stone's Best Picture winner Platoon (1986) is set during which war?
AnswerDetails: Stone drew on his own service as an infantryman in Vietnam to write and direct Platoon.

Title: The Last Emperor (1987) won every Oscar it was nominated for. How many was that?
AnswerDetails: Bernardo Bertolucci's film about Puyi, China's last emperor, went nine for nine, including Best Picture.

Title: Rain Man won Best Picture for 1988. Who won Best Actor for playing Raymond Babbitt?
AnswerDetails: Dustin Hoffman won his second Best Actor Oscar; Tom Cruise played Raymond's brother Charlie.

Title: At 80, Jessica Tandy became the oldest Best Actress winner up to that time. For which 1989 film?
AnswerDetails: Tandy won for playing Daisy Werthan; Driving Miss Daisy also won Best Picture.

Title: Best Picture winner Chariots of Fire (1981) follows British runners competing at which Olympic Games?
AnswerDetails: The film follows Harold Abrahams and Eric Liddell on their way to the 1924 Games in Paris.

Title: In The Color of Money (1986), which won Paul Newman his first competitive Oscar, what does his character "Fast Eddie" Felson play?
AnswerDetails: Newman reprised the pool hustler he first played in The Hustler (1961), this time mentoring Tom Cruise.

Title: Who won Best Supporting Actor for playing retired astronaut Garrett Breedlove in Terms of Endearment (1983)?
AnswerDetails: Nicholson won Best Supporting Actor; the film also won Best Picture and Best Actress for Shirley MacLaine.

Title: Which actor won Best Director for his very first film behind the camera, Ordinary People (1980)?
AnswerDetails: Robert Redford won Best Director for his debut, and Ordinary People won Best Picture.

Title: Survivor's "Eye of the Tiger" was written for which film?
AnswerDetails: Sylvester Stallone asked Survivor for a new theme for Rocky III (1982); the song topped the US charts.

Title: Ben E. King's "Stand by Me" returned to the charts with the 1986 film of the same name. Whose story was the film adapted from?
AnswerDetails: Rob Reiner adapted Stephen King's novella "The Body" (1982), and the 1961 song became a hit all over again.

Title: Who sang the title song of Footloose (1984)?
AnswerDetails: Kenny Loggins co-wrote and sang "Footloose," which reached No. 1 in the US.

Title: Simple Minds' "Don't You (Forget About Me)" plays over the opening and closing of which film?
AnswerDetails: The song was written for The Breakfast Club (1985) and became Simple Minds' biggest US hit.

Title: Who sang "Flashdance... What a Feeling," which won the Oscar for Best Original Song?
AnswerDetails: Irene Cara sang it and shared the songwriting Oscar with Giorgio Moroder and Keith Forsey.

Title: Which band recorded "The Power of Love" for Back to the Future?
AnswerDetails: Huey Lewis and the News took it to No. 1 in the US; Lewis also has a cameo as a battle-of-the-bands judge.

Title: Which composer scored E.T., Raiders of the Lost Ark and The Empire Strikes Back?
AnswerDetails: John Williams scored all three; The Empire Strikes Back introduced his "Imperial March."

Title: Which composer won the Oscar for the synthesizer score of Chariots of Fire?
AnswerDetails: The Greek composer Vangelis won Best Original Score, and his opening theme became a worldwide hit.

Title: Public Enemy's "Fight the Power" was recorded for which 1989 film?
AnswerDetails: Spike Lee asked Public Enemy for an anthem, and the song plays throughout Do the Right Thing.

Title: Who composed "Axel F," the synth theme from Beverly Hills Cop?
AnswerDetails: Harold Faltermeyer wrote it; Jan Hammer's similar-sounding hit was the Miami Vice theme.
